title: Bank of England MPC decision, vote split AND the annual QT review (12:00 London / 07:00 ET; no Monetary Policy Report)
source: EST: bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 — the 2026 announcement list reads '5 February (MPR) · 19 March · 30 April (MPR) · 18 June · 30 July (MPR) · 17 September · 5 November (MPR) · 17 December', with 17 September flagged as the next scheduled announcement and carrying NO Monetary Policy Report; the Bank's own September-2026 minutes page is live as 'to be published at 12pm'. Corroborated from a second, independent BoE primary: the Asset Purchase Facility gilt-sales Market Notice of 19 June 2026 states verbatim that future sales schedules will follow 'the MPC's annual review ... which is expected to be announced alongside the MPC meeting on 17 September 2026'. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has FED: and no slot for a non-Fed central bank — the same gap ecb-decision-2026-09-10 and boj-decision-2026-09-18 were filed under. The date is the Bank's own; the 12:00 London time is press-relayed. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-09, superseding proposals/boe-decision-2026-09-17.from-fomc-2026-09-16.json (the FOMC lane's D-7 sweep discovery, read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md). That proposal's placement finding stands and is kept: the MPC MEETING ENDS 09-16, the same day as the FOMC statement, so the corridor is FOMC 09-16 14:00 ET -> BoE 09-17 07:00 ET -> BoJ 09-18, and a gilt move on 09-17 is no longer automatically attributable to Fed spillover. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDED, AND IT CHANGES THE PAYLOAD: the rate decision is near-dead information (centralbank.watch, fetched 2026-09-08: HOLD 93.1% / hike 6.9% / cut 0.0%, implied 3.77% against Bank Rate 3.75%), but this is the meeting that carries the BANK'S ANNUAL QT REVIEW — the gilt-stock reduction target for October 2026 to September 2027, successor to the GBP 70bn target set in September 2025. That is a SUPPLY decision, published into a 30-year gilt at 5.89% (early September 2026, highest since March 1998) and a 2056 gilt sold 2026-09-08 at 5.8168%, the highest yield at any DMO auction since the office was founded in 1998. Consensus is a slowdown to GBP 50bn (market-participant median). Tiered medium and NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED: symbols: [], no house playbook is rates-keyed, no tracked name carries sterling-rates exposure. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
